articles.headline: OFAC Amends Venezuela-Related General License for Earthquake Relief
body: The U.S. Department of the Treasury's Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) has issued Venezuela-related General License (GL) 60A, titled "Authorizing Transactions Related to Earthquake Relief Efforts in Venezuela." This amended license supersedes GL 60, issued on June 25, 2026, and authorizes all transactions related to earthquake relief efforts in Venezuela that would otherwise be prohibited by the Venezuela Sanctions Regulations (VSR) through April 21, 2027.

The authorization in GL 60A includes the processing or transfer of funds on behalf of third-country persons to or from Venezuela in support of these authorized transactions. U.S. financial institutions and registered money transmitters can rely on the originator of a funds transfer for compliance, provided they do not know or have reason to know that the transfer is not in compliance.

However, this general license does not authorize the unblocking of any property blocked under the VSR or any other transactions prohibited by other Executive Orders or parts of 31 CFR chapter V not referenced in the license. OFAC also issued one amended Frequently Asked Question, FAQ 1263, in conjunction with this action.

articles.headline: OFAC Designates Iranian and Cuban Entities, Issues New General Licenses
body: The U.S. Department of the Treasury's Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) announced new Iran-related designations, a Cuba designation, and the issuance of new and amended General Licenses and Frequently Asked Questions. The action targets 16 Iran-related individuals and multiple enterprises and financial institutions, including Iraq's International Development Bank for Investment and Finance, Iran's Chabahar International Offshore Bank, Jazireh International Bank, and several currency exchange companies.

Concurrently, OFAC designated Cuba's state-owned Banco Internacional de Comercio S.A. (BICSA) for providing financial services to Iranian banks. This designation was made pursuant to Executive Order (E.O.) 14404, which targets the financial services sector of the Cuban economy.

In addition to the designations, OFAC issued Russia-related General License 128D, authorizing certain transactions involving Lukoil retail service stations outside of Russia, and Russia-related General License 130B, authorizing transactions involving certain Lukoil entities in Bulgaria. An Iran-related General License FF was also issued, authorizing the wind down of transactions involving the International Development Bank for Investment and Finance. OFAC also released a new Cuba-related FAQ (FAQ 1276) and an amended Russia-related FAQ (FAQ 1225).

articles.headline: OFAC Removes Venezuelan National Assembly President from Sanctions List
body: The U.S. Department of the Treasury's Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) has removed Jorge Jesús Rodríguez Gómez, the president of Venezuela's National Assembly, from its Specially Designated Nationals and Blocked Persons (SDN) List. This action covers Rodríguez and the alternative names associated with his designation under the Venezuela sanctions program.

Rodríguez, who has led the National Assembly since 2021, was originally designated on September 25, 2018, under Executive Order 13692 for being an official of the Venezuelan government. His sister, Delcy Rodríguez, Venezuela's acting president, was also delisted in April 2026.

This removal is part of a broader diplomatic effort by Washington and follows a three-phase plan for Venezuela's stabilization and political transition, which includes ongoing government-opposition talks.

articles.headline: OFAC Targets Cartel del Noreste's Horse Racing Enterprise and Criminal Network
body: The U.S. Department of the Treasury's Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) has announced Counter Narcotics and Counter Terrorism Designations, targeting individuals and entities associated with the Cartel del Noreste (CDN) in Mexico. This action aims to disrupt the cartel's financial network, particularly its involvement in horse racing.

Among the designated individuals are Gamaliel Garza Elias and Gamaliel Garza Garcia, both linked to the CDN. Several entities, including Club La Molienda (also known as La Molienda Race Track), Concretos y Productos Asfalticos del Norte, S.A. de C.V., Cuadra San DibanH, and Distribuidora de Gas Economico, S.A. de C.V., were also added to the Specially Designated Nationals (SDN) List.

These designations fall under Executive Order 13224, as amended by Executive Order 13886, and Executive Order 14059, which target global terrorism and illicit drug trafficking. The action highlights the U.S. government's ongoing efforts to combat transnational criminal organizations and their financial facilitators.

articles.headline: OFAC Designates International Criminal Court, Issues General Licenses
body: The U.S. Department of the Treasury's Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) has designated the International Criminal Court (ICC) and issued several related General Licenses. This action places the ICC on the Specially Designated Nationals (SDN) List, effectively imposing institution-wide sanctions.

In conjunction with the designation, OFAC issued four General Licenses: GL 13, "Authorizing Certain Transactions Involving the International Criminal Court"; GL 14, "Authorizing Certain Transactions Related to Telecommunications and Enterprise Software Involving the International Criminal Court"; GL 15, "Authorizing Transactions Related to Pension Payments Involving the International Criminal Court"; and GL 16, "Authorizing Certain Transactions Related to Certain International Criminal Court Detainees." These licenses provide narrow exceptions to the sanctions.

The designation of the ICC follows previous U.S. sanctions targeting individuals associated with the court and is a significant escalation in the Trump administration's campaign against the institution. The U.S. government justified the action as necessary to protect American sovereignty.

articles.headline: OFAC Issues Russia-Related General License for Diesel Fuel
body: The U.S. Department of the Treasury's Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) has issued Russia-related General License (GL) 135, titled "Authorizing Transactions Related to the Sale, Delivery, Offloading, and Importation of Diesel Fuel of Russian Federation Origin." This license temporarily authorizes certain transactions that would otherwise be prohibited under the Russian Harmful Foreign Activities Sanctions Regulations and the Ukraine-/Russia-Related Sanctions Regulations.

The authorization, which includes importation into the United States, is effective through April 7, 2027. It covers commercial activities related to the delivery and sale of Russian-origin diesel fuel.

This move comes amidst ongoing regional instability and follows a presidential announcement regarding the release of Russian diesel fuel to global markets. While intended to potentially ease global energy market pressures, the legal implications of this GL in relation to existing congressional import bans are subject to debate.
articles.source: U.S. Treasury OFAC / Diplomacy and Law

articles.headline: OFAC Designates Iran-Related Individuals and Entities, Amends Russia GL
body: The U.S. Department of the Treasury's Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) has announced new Iran-related designations and the issuance of an Iran-related General License, alongside an amended Russia-related General License. The designations target several individuals and entities under Executive Order 13846 and Executive Order 13902, which focus on Iran's financial and petroleum sectors.

Among the designated individuals are Harishyam Hariharan Chundakattil, Said Ahmad Noorzad, Bhupendrasingh Dhalsingh Sahu, Dhwani Nisarg Vora, and Nisarg Samir Vora, all linked to activities supporting the Iranian regime. Entities added to the SDN list include Goddess Shipping Corp. and Gravion Maritime Co.

OFAC also issued Iran-related General License EE, authorizing the wind down of transactions involving Samudra Marine Services Private Limited. Additionally, Russia-related General License 13S was issued, authorizing certain administrative transactions prohibited by Directive 4 under Executive Order 14024.

articles.headline: OFAC Publishes Iran-Related Alert and FAQ Amendments
body: The U.S. Department of the Treasury's Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) has announced designations removals and updates, along with the publication of an Iran-related OFAC Alert and an amended Iran-related Frequently Asked Question. This action reflects ongoing adjustments to sanctions lists and guidance concerning Iran.

The Iran-related OFAC Alert provides updated information and warnings regarding sanctions risks associated with transactions involving Iran. The amended Frequently Asked Question offers clarifications on existing Iran sanctions policies.

These updates are part of OFAC's continuous effort to maintain the effectiveness and clarity of its sanctions programs, ensuring that U.S. persons and foreign entities are aware of their compliance obligations.

articles.headline: OFAC Announces New Counter Terrorism Designations
body: The U.S. Department of the Treasury's Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) has announced new Counter Terrorism Designations. These actions are part of ongoing efforts to disrupt the financial networks of terrorist organizations and their supporters globally.

While specific details of the designated individuals or entities were not immediately released in the summary, such designations typically involve blocking property and interests in property of those found to have engaged in, or posed a significant risk of materially contributing to, acts of terrorism.
These designations underscore the U.S. government's commitment to combating terrorism financing and protecting the international financial system from illicit activities.

articles.headline: Bank of America Settles with OFAC for $11.6 Million Over Sanctions Violations
body: Bank of America, N.A. has agreed to pay $11,662,930 to settle its potential civil liability for 475 apparent violations of multiple OFAC sanctions programs. These violations involved sanctions targeting Russia, Belarus, Iran, Burma, Somalia, narcotics, and global terrorism.

The apparent violations occurred when Bank of America processed payments involving blocked banks, failed to appropriately prioritize alerts for customers matching blocked persons, did not promptly update watchlists following OFAC designations, and mishandled business accounts associated with blocked persons due to human error. The total value of these apparent violations was approximately $14,834,082.

OFAC determined that the apparent violations were non-egregious but largely not voluntarily self-disclosed. The settlement amount reflects no reduction to the base penalty, including no mitigation for remedial measures or cooperation, though Bank of America has made significant compliance commitments.

articles.headline: Pegasus Worldwide Logistics Settles with OFAC for $175,015
body: Pegasus Worldwide Logistics, a California-based freight forwarding firm, has agreed to pay $175,015 to settle its potential civil liability for apparent violations of the Illicit Drug Trafficking Sanctions Regulations and the Reporting, Procedures and Penalties Regulations. The settlement resolves four apparent violations of dealing in blocked property and six apparent violations related to an incomplete response to an administrative subpoena.

Between September 2023 and February 2024, Pegasus facilitated the importation of a machine supplied by a designated company, Youli Technology Development Co., Ltd., which had been sanctioned under Executive Order 14059 for its involvement in counterfeit pill production. Pegasus failed to identify the designated supplier due to deficiencies in its compliance program and also failed to fully respond to an OFAC subpoena for six months.

OFAC determined that Pegasus's conduct was non-egregious and not voluntarily disclosed. The settlement amount reflects consideration of aggravating factors, including the failure to screen available identifiers and the delay caused by the incomplete subpoena response, as well as Pegasus's extensive remedial measures.

The settlement underscores OFAC's continued enforcement efforts against individuals who violate sanctions regulations, regardless of whether the violations are egregious or voluntarily disclosed.

articles.headline: Streamlining Export Controls for Drone Exports
body: The Bureau of Industry and Security (BIS) is easing export controls on certain Unmanned Aerial Vehicles (UAVs or drones) and related parts, components, accessories, attachments, technology, and software under the Export Administration Regulations (EAR). Specifically, this rule: eliminates wind gust tolerance as a parameter for determining UAV controls under the EAR; increases the threshold for national security controls on certain UAVs from an endurance of 30 minutes to an endurance of 3 hours; makes conforming changes to remove national security controls on software and technology associated with UAVs with an endurance less than 3 hours; maintains military end-use and end-user controls on those lower endurance drones and associated software and technology; clarifies Commerce Control List (CCL) controls for certain UAVs specially designed for military use; and removes national security controls on certain specially designed parts, components, accessories, and attachments for such UAVs as they do not provide any significant military or intelligence capabilities.

articles.headline: Implementation of EAR Export Controls on Silencers, Mufflers, and Sound Suppressors; and Other Firearms Related Changes
body: The Department of Commerce (Commerce), Bureau of Industry and Security (BIS) is revising the Export Administration Regulations (EAR) and the Commerce Control List (CCL) to appropriately control certain silencers, mufflers, and sound suppressors (sound suppressors) that will no longer be described on the International Traffic in Arms Regulations U.S. Munitions List (USML). This interim final rule (IFR) complements a Department of State interim final rule published elsewhere in this issue of the Federal Register (International Traffic in Arms Regulations: USML Category I Firearm Suppressors (1400-AG11) (State IFR)). This transfer of jurisdiction will reduce the regulatory burden on exports of sound suppressors. This IFR also revises the EAR to allow firearms and related items to be temporarily exported and reexported under a license exception as tools of trade, thereby relieving exporters of the regulatory burden of applying for authorization. Finally, this IFR clarifies which items fall within the scope of the EAR's entry clearance requirements for a temporary import.

articles.headline: Enhanced Favorable Treatment for the United Arab Emirates Under the Export Administration Regulations
body: In this final rule, the Bureau of Industry and Security (BIS) amends the Export Administration Regulations (EAR) to provide enhanced favorable treatment for the United Arab Emirates (UAE). Specifically, BIS is removing the UAE from Country Groups D:3 and D:4 and adding the UAE to Country Group A:5. More license exceptions will now be available, including Strategic Trade Authorization (STA) for the UAE Government and approved commercial entities in the UAE. STA will authorize the export, reexport, or transfer (in-country) of military items; certain commercial satellites and spacecraft; and dual-use items useful in, inter alia, oil and gas production, desalination, and civil nuclear power generation. The UAE Government and approved commercial entities will also have license-free access to advanced computing items, consistent with the May 2025 U.S.-UAE Artificial Intelligence Cooperation framework, without compromising U.S. digital infrastructure buildout.

articles.headline: Trump calls off livestream of Fort Hood attacker's execution by firing squad
body: Trump said some would "rather not watch" the killing of Nidal Hasan, the first military execution in over 60 years.

articles.headline: Tip-off foiled US teen suspect's plot to attack Hindu temple, police say
body: The alleged plot only failed because the 19-year-old suspect's gun jammed outside the place of worship, say police.

articles.headline: Bus hits train stopped on French side of Channel Tunnel, with 19 injured
body: Two people were airlifted to hospital but no-one's life appeared to be in danger, officials said.

articles.headline: Maduro pleads not guilty to new torture-related charges in New York
body: "I reject this document entirely," Maduro said in court, responding to newly added torture-related charges.

articles.headline: Houthi missile attack on Yemeni presidential palace kills five, minister says
body: Yemen's information minister says the prime minister and other ministers were unhurt when ballistic missiles hit al-Maashiq Palace.

articles.headline: Seven crew missing after drone attack leaves tanker ablaze off Romania's coast
body: A search and rescue operation is under way in the Black Sea after the latest attack in the area.

articles.headline: White House defends new press secretary over her legal credentials
body: Katie Zacharia does not appear to be registered to the legal bar in any state where she has lived.

articles.headline: School headscarf ban sparks rare protests in Azerbaijan and row with Turkey
body: Protests have taken place over the rules which have seen pupils wearing hijabs turned away from schools.

articles.headline: Letters with 'suspicious substances' sent to US senators and election offices
body: A number of states have confirmed they were targeted by the mailings, including Oklahoma, Ohio and Louisiana.

articles.headline: Two dead in Istanbul after heaviest rainfall in 84 years, governor says
body: Residents have been told to avoid leaving their homes unless absolutely necessary.

articles.headline: Obama says drift towards extremism 'not inevitable'
body: More than 12,000 people filled a major venue in the city to hear the former US president's take on the challenges the world is facing. .
